text:
Anya: heads up — we saw a 3x jump in preemptions in eu-west3 between 09:10–09:40 UTC. eviction_rate is spiking but single-signal alerts are noisy :thinking:
Matt: can you paste the current dashboard? is SLO actually impacted or just transient?
Anya: dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/spot-eu-west3-heatmap — most requests still within latency SLO but tail tokens have increased. I'm proposing a composite 'spot_health' score that fuses multiple signals so we only alert when there's real SLO risk.
Jamie: love the idea. which signals do you want to combine?
Anya: minimal set: eviction_rate (1m/5m), median_time_to_eviction (TTE), instance_launch_failures, avg_queue_wait_ms, spare_capacity_index (from cloud API), recent_price_delta. weight them and smooth. Also include burstiness/variance so short blips don't trigger paging.
Matt: OK. we should map the composite score to SLO buckets: 
- score >= 0.7 -> page oncall (SLO degradation likely)
- 0.4 <= score < 0.7 -> notify #eng-infra-ops, create incident record but no page
- < 0.4 -> emit metric only, no noisy alerts
Kevin: paging threshold seems fine. add region and pool dimensions so we can triage per mixed-capacity pool (preemptible vs reserved).
Jamie: implementation note: keep label cardinality low. roll up by region+gpu_type+pool_role. do not include instance_id in the composite rule.
Anya: agreed. rough Prometheus alert prototype below (will refine):
```yaml
groups:
- name: spot-health.rules
  rules:
  - alert: SpotHealthDegraded
    expr: >-
      (0.4*avg_over_time(eviction_rate[5m]) + 0.25*(1 - avg_over_time(tte_seconds[5m]) / scalar(300)) + 0.15*avg_over_time(launch_failures[5m]) + 0.2*(1 - spare_capacity_index)) > 0.7
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "Composite spot health degraded in {{ $labels.region }} / {{ $labels.gpu_type }}"
```
Matt: nice. for the Grafana heatmap we'll surface per-pool score and interruption-rate over last 12h, plus a sparkline for price_delta. Query example: `sum by (region, pool_role) (rate(ec2_spot_interruption_count[5m])) / sum by (region, pool_role) (instance_count)`
Jamie: how do we avoid alert storms across pools when there's a global cloud maintenance event? maybe add a global suppressor if global_interruptions_ratio > 0.6.
Anya: yes — use an ops-bot mute rule: if global_spot_eviction_ratio > 0.6 then lower alerts to notify-only for 30m. ops-bot will post a summary + ETA from cloud provider.
ops-bot: automated note — subscribed to cloud interruption webhooks. will emit `cloud_spot_interruption_webhook` metric and tag origin.
sre-bot: reminder: correlate with latency_slo_breach metric before paging. the pager should include the current composite score, recent eviction_rate, and recommended fallback (e.g., move 10% traffic to dedicated).
Kevin: fallback policy idea: ramp percentage to dedicated pool with circuit-breaker and cooldown. runbook command (pseudo):
```bash
# shift 10% of traffic from spot-pool-a to dedicated-pool-1
redwoodctl route modify --from pool:spot-pool-a --to pool:dedicated-pool-1 --percent 10 --reason "spot health composite >= 0.7"
```
Jamie: we also need a cost guardrail — if fallback increases cost beyond X% of baseline, generate a review alert rather than full failover.
Anya: implementation plan:
1) instrument new metrics (spare_capacity_index, launch_failures) and webhook pipeline — Kevin + Jamie
2) build composite metric in Prometheus using a moving-average window and exponential smoothing — Matt
3) deploy to staging + run 2-week canary comparing alert noise vs current rules — Anya (owner)
4) if successful, roll to prod with a new dashboard and updated runbooks — rotate oncall trainings
Matt: timeline?
Anya: target PRs this week, staging deploy early next, canary for 2 weeks. I'll own the rollout.
Kevin: I'll scope the webhook and region label work.
Jamie: I'll do the alert rule review and check label cardinality.
Matt: +1. Also add a daily cron job to recompute baseline weights for the composite (traffic patterns shift).
Anya: quick question — retention window for the composite metric? thinking 90d for analysis, 14d for alerting baselines. thoughts?
Jamie: 90d analysis, keep 14d moving baseline sounds reasonable. keep low-res longer, high-res for 14d.
Kevin: cost note: if we observe repeated fallbacks, we should evaluate increasing reserved capacity per region — flag for finance/pm.
Anya: cool. I'll open the tracking ticket and add the dashboard mockups. tagging @Matt @Jamie @Kevin for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
